note: The edit and view boards. `sections` is the whole view-model: seven sections, four block kinds. Every field carries the `path` a form posts it under.

synthesised.reporting.partner_feed_agreement: Not implemented on this instance. Synthesised into the profile's parameters exactly as 09a-fixtures-dump.php does for palette.json, so the edit board's own fixture carries the `missing` state the brief requires it to draw. The item is the tool's output, copied from palette.json rather than composed. AnalystProfileFormTool already emits it: sectionSignals() calls signalPalette(), which unions the catalogue with the profile's entries.

profile.name: Weights I actually use
profile.description: The instance default Analyst Profile. Phase 2 authored the eleven-signal catalogue and its weights against the regression set: the four demo values anchor the shape, the median value (one org, no sightings) fixes the calibration rule. Phase 5 completed the relevance section: the clock, the curve at decay_speed 1, and the per-type TTL table, which errs generous because a short TTL drops indicators silently and a long one merely fails to flag a stale one. Phase 6 added reference.org_trust_scale, the admiralty grade multipliers, with both override maps still empty: an empty org_trust map switches trust weighting off entirely, so this profile scores exactly as it did before the section existed. See prd/analyst-profile/03-signals.md section 7, 06-staleness.md section 3 and 07-reference.md section 2.3.

thresholds.title: Thresholds
thresholds.blurb: Where the counted evidence turns into a word. The lean asks how one-sided the record is; the bands ask how much of it there is.

fields.label: Supermajority share
fields.help: The share of organisations that must agree before the record is read as asserting one thing. A supermajority on either side, with a tolerance — 34 of 100 against misses the mirror of 0.66 by a floating-point hair.

fields.label: Signals needed for high
fields.help: What stops one heavy row buying a high band on its own.

blocks.title: The thin-record clamp
blocks.blurb: A ceiling on the band for a record with one source and nothing corroborating it. The weights alone cannot express this: one organisation reporting the same value for fourteen months sums past any floor that still says something useful about the values that do have corroboration. Delete the three numbers to remove the clamp.

fields.label: Sources that still count as one
Sightings that still count as none

escalations.title: Conflict rules
escalations.blurb: When the record contradicts itself loudly enough that no lean is honest. A rule may only ever say contested — one that could name a side would be a score override wearing a different hat.

items.title: conflict:known-infrastructure-vs-reporting
items.description: A warninglist knows the value as shared infrastructure while several organisations report it as a threat.

fields.label: The category of list that must match

items.title: conflict:listed-vs-asserted
items.description: A list marks the value as a false positive while a supermajority of organisations report it as a threat.

fields.label: The category of list that must match
Share of organisations asserting it, as a fraction or the word supermajority

exclusions.title: Exclusions
exclusions.blurb: Evidence you have decided not to count, filtered before any signal sees it — so two signals reading the same fact read the same filtered set. Every row an exclusion removes is listed in the assessment as not counted, naming the rule.

items.title: Self-sightings
items.description: An organisation confirming its own fresh report is not corroboration. Sightings filed by the reporting organisation within the window below are left out; later ones are kept, because "we still see this" is real information.

items.title: Mirrored feeds
items.description: Feeds sharing another's source counted once rather than separately. MISP does not record what a feed mirrors, so this folds by the key below — which is wrong where one provider runs unrelated feeds.

items.title: Your own organisation
items.description: Leave your own organisation out of every count, so the assessment says what everyone else reports. This one changes the queries rather than filtering their results, so it moves every aggregate at once.

items.title: Evidence window
items.description: On a value with more occurrences than the threshold, read row evidence from the last N days only. Whole-history aggregates are never windowed. Applied by the context builder rather than here, because it decides what is fetched.

relevance.title: Relevance
relevance.blurb: Whether what the record asserts still matters today. Its own axis, and nothing in the quality reads it: silence must never be able to promote a value to a definite answer.

fields.label: Measure from
fields.help: Last independent corroboration is somebody other than the original reporter saying it again. Newest occurrence is the fallback where nothing else can be dated.

fields.label: Decay speed
fields.help: MISP's polynomial. 1 is linear; exponential has no TTL to measure against, which is why the curve is pinned here.

fields.label: Aging from
fields.help: The share of the TTL left when a value stops reading as current.

fields.label: Encoding lag before uncertain
fields.help: An encoding date is later than the observation it stands for, so time measured from it is a lower bound. Past this lag the timeline is flagged uncertain — which is the common state on real data, not the exotic one.

blocks.title: Time to live, per type
blocks.blurb: How long a report of this type stays current without corroboration. Only the types you have an opinion about; everything else follows the default.

reference.title: Reference data
reference.blurb: What you believe about your sources, and what the warninglists mean. Admiralty-shaped on purpose: source reliability goes in, information credibility comes out.

blocks.title: Organisation trust
blocks.blurb: Admiralty grades. F is neutral, the same as C — the shipped taxonomy says so — and G is deliberately deceptive and worth nothing. Only the organisations you have graded.

blocks.title: What a grade is worth
blocks.blurb: The multiplier each grade contributes. A voice graded E counts as a quarter of one.

blocks.title: Warninglist categories
blocks.blurb: What a list hit means: known infrastructure is not a false positive. Nothing upstream sets this column yet, so the instance ships a map and this is where you disagree with it.

enrichment.title: Enrichment
enrichment.blurb: Which modules you would want asked about a value of each type. Nothing runs on its own: the tab arrives with these ticked and a run still takes a press.

fields.label: Modules that may be offered
fields.help: Whether a module that would tell somebody outside this instance the value is being looked at may be offered. Local only selects very little on a platform where enrichment mostly means asking somebody else, and says so. Not a cost setting: nothing a module declares says anything about money or rate limits.

fields.label: Reuse an answer for
fields.help: Inert: there is no store of module answers, so nothing is reused and this window governs nothing yet.

blocks.title: Where a module answers from
blocks.blurb: Overrides the shipped roster. Locality cannot be derived — a module that declares no config and no requirements may still fetch a third-party site — so it ships as knowledge and this is where you correct it.
